rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Replacing a substring with itself has no effect and may indicate a mistake.

rules.cwe_name: Assignment to Variable without Use
rules.description: If two functions with the same name are declared in the same scope, one of the declarations overrides the other without warning. This makes the code hard to read and maintain, and may even lead to platform-dependent behavior.

rules.cwe_name: Use of Potentially Dangerous Function
rules.description: DOM functions that act like 'eval' and execute strings as code are dangerous and impede program analysis and understanding. Consequently, they should not be used.

rules.cwe_name: Dead Code
rules.description: If a dollar assertion '$' appears in a regular expression before another term that cannot match the empty string, then this assertion can never match, so the entire regular expression cannot match any string.

rules.cwe_name: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
rules.description: Using a cryptographically weak pseudo-random number generator to generate a security-sensitive value may allow an attacker to predict what value will be generated.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
rules.description: External links that open in a new tab or window but do not specify link type 'noopener' or 'noreferrer' are a potential security risk.

rules.cwe_name: Creation of Temporary File With Insecure Permissions
rules.description: Creating a temporary file that is accessible by other users can lead to information disclosure and sometimes remote code execution.

rules.cwe_name: Expression is Always True
rules.description: Comparing the result of a typeof test against a string other than 'undefined', 'boolean', 'number', 'string', 'object', 'function' or 'symbol' is useless, since this comparison can never succeed.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
rules.description: Recursively merging a user-controlled object into another object can allow an attacker to modify the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
rules.description: Instantiating a template using a user-controlled object is vulnerable to local file read and potential remote code execution.

rules.cwe_name: Storage of File with Sensitive Data Under Web Root
rules.description: Exposing a node_modules folder, or the project folder to the public, can cause exposure of private information.

rules.cwe_name: Inclusion of Web Functionality from an Untrusted Source
rules.description: Using a resource from an untrusted or compromised domain makes your code vulnerable to receiving malicious code.

rules.cwe_name: Off-by-one Error
rules.description: An array index is compared to be less than or equal to the 'length' property, and then used in an indexing operation that could be out of bounds.

rules.cwe_name: Numeric Truncation Error
rules.description: The integer shift operators '<<', '>>' and '>>>' only take the five least significant bits of their right operand into account. Thus, it is not possible to shift an integer by more than 31 bits.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Input Validation
rules.description: Matching a URL or hostname against a regular expression that contains an unescaped dot as part of the hostname might match more hostnames than expected.
